title: How to Get Rich: Naval on specific knowledge, accountability, leverage and judgment
summary: Naval walks through his "How to Get Rich" tweetstorm. Wealth is owned assets that earn while you sleep, built with specific knowledge, accountability, leverage and judgment, not rented time. Code and media are permissionless leverage, and long-term games with ethical, high-integrity partners compound. Also covers business models (network effects, scale economies, price discrimination) and hourly-rate discipline.

principles.text: Own equity; you can't get rich renting out your time because inputs match outputs.
principles.quote: You are not going to get rich renting out your time. You must own equity, a piece of the business to gain your financial freedom.

principles.text: Get paid for building what society wants but can't yet get, then scale it to millions.
principles.quote: you want to figure out which one of those things you can provide for society, that it does not yet know how to get, but it will want, that’s natural to you, and within your skillset

principles.text: Code and media are permissionless, zero-marginal-cost leverage; use minimal labor to get them.
principles.quote: The most interesting and the most important form of leverage is this idea of products that have no marginal cost of replication. This is the new form of leverage.

principles.text: Pick a business model with network effects, low marginal costs and scale economies; get users to add value to each other.
principles.quote: You should always be thinking about how your users, your customers, can add value to each other because that is the ultimate form of leverage.

principles.text: Escape competition by being authentic; copying drags you into a lesser game.
principles.quote: Authenticity naturally gets you away from competition. ... Competition leads to copy-catting and playing the completely wrong game.

principles.text: Price discrimination: charge by propensity to pay, but give the high payers something extra they value.
principles.quote: Price discrimination is important. It means you can charge people based on their propensity to pay.
